rounds.proof_sketch: Kernel launched with `dim3 blocks(batch_size * num_groups)` and `threads_per_block=256` as scalar integer, creating 1D thread blocks where blockDim=(256,1,1). Thus threadIdx.z=0 for ALL 256 threads. Original condition `threadIdx.x==0` true for 1 thread; mutated `threadIdx.z==0` true for ALL threads. Post-reduction, shared_data[0] contains identical value visible to all threads. All threads compute same var=shared_data[0]/group_elements and inv_std=rsqrtf(var+eps), then all write same value to shared_data[0]. Multiple threads writing identical value = single thread writing. After __syncthreads(), correct inv_std is available.
rounds.survival_reason: The kernel is launched with 1D thread blocks (blockDim.x=256, blockDim.y=1, blockDim.z=1). This means threadIdx.z is always 0 for every thread in every block. The mutation changes the gating condition from 'only thread 0 executes' (threadIdx.x==0) to 'all threads execute' (threadIdx.z==0). However, this is semantically equivalent because: (1) after the variance reduction completes, shared_data[0] holds the same sum for all threads, (2) all 256 threads compute identical var and inv_std values from this shared data, (3) all threads write the same value to shared_data[0], which is a benign data race producing the correct result. The __syncthreads() ensures all threads see the final correct inv_std value before proceeding.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. The equivalence is structural, not value-dependent: 1D thread blocks guarantee threadIdx.z=0 always, and deterministic identical writes from multiple threads produce the same result as a single write. No input values can change the thread block dimensionality or make threads compute different inv_std values from the same shared reduction result.
rounds.recommendations: To detect such structurally-equivalent mutations, the testing framework should either: (1) analyze kernel launch configurations to identify when threadIdx.y/z swaps are semantically equivalent in 1D launches, or (2) instrument kernels to count how many threads execute gated sections and flag changed thread counts even when outputs match.
